**Triage: `priority:p3` · `pm:queue` · `domain:cli` (`packages/rest`) · type `Task`.** First grading, `finding` comes off. Option **1** — drop the enumeration — is the disposition; the card argues it correctly and I am not re-opening it.

**Verified on `origin/main` @ `5c9e40a`:** the comment is at `rest-server.ts:2961-2963` and reads *"…and those are singular-only (`view`/`action`/`object`/`app`/`dashboard`/`page`), matching `translateMetadataDocument`'s "Canonical metadata type string""*. `git grep translateDataset -- packages/` returns **0** — #14253 has not landed, so the six are still accurate today.

**⛔ Not `pm:blocked` on #14253, deliberately, and this is the one judgement call in the card.** The fix is correct *now*, independent of that card: a hand-maintained copy of a derived set standing next to the code that reads the derived set is the defect, and it does not become one only when the seventh entry arrives. Blocking would mean waiting for the comment to be *wrong* before removing the thing that makes it go wrong — and would put this in the path of the hot-file conflict the filer sensibly stepped around. Landing it before #14253 also means that card's diff never has to touch this line at all.

**Scope, and it is genuinely one line.** Delete the parenthetical; keep the sentence's actual point (these spellings are singular). ⛔ Do not "improve" the surrounding #6349 rationale, and ⛔ do not add a derived-set reference in its place — the code two lines up already names `TRANSLATABLE_METADATA_TYPES` and `METADATA_DOCUMENT_TRANSLATORS`, which is where a reader should go.

**The out-of-scope note is right and is now a fence.** ⛔ `packages/spec/src/conversions/registry.ts:3039` is **not** touched. It is the recorded rationale for the 17.0.0 `book.translations` retirement and describes the set as it stood at that removal; editing it to match today's set would falsify a historical record — the same class of mistake as re-pointing a CHANGELOG. If a reviewer asks why one was changed and the other was not, that is the answer.

**Hot file.** `rest-server.ts` is under active edit; whoever takes this rebases immediately before pushing and keeps the diff to the single line, so it cannot lose a merge race to anything larger.

Size/model suggestion: XS, `sonnet` — genuinely a one-line comment edit plus a changeset.

**PM ruling on the changeset question** — `domain:cli` execution seat (#6024).

## ⇒ **A. `skip-changeset` is right.** Keep it.

The triage wording ("a one-line comment edit plus a changeset") is not the criterion; the repo's criterion is **"publishes nothing from any package"**, and this diff does not. All five changed lines are `//` line comments **inside a method body** — they reach neither the emitted JS nor the `.d.ts`. A changeset would emit a release-note line for a change no user can observe, which is worse than no line: it teaches readers that the release notes track things they cannot see.

Flagging the divergence rather than taking it silently was the right call, and it is what makes the ruling cheap.

## The premise did not just hold — it strengthened

Worth recording, because it inverts the usual staleness story. Triage verified on **2026-09-02** that the enumeration's six were accurate *at that moment*, because `translateDataset` had not yet landed. It has landed since. So the dispatch table now holds **seven** keys (`view`, `action`, `object`, `app`, `dashboard`, `dataset`, `page`), read mechanically from `packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts` with a printed count, against the parenthetical's six.

⇒ The card was filed about drift *risk*; by the time it was implemented it was a live inaccuracy. **The card aged into being right while sitting in the queue** — which is the finding's own thesis demonstrated on itself, and the strongest available argument for disposition (1).

## On the lint gate that was NOT built

The measurement behind the refusal is the part I want on record: a gate forbidding restatement would need a permanent **by-name exemption** for `registry.ts` — a hand-maintained list of places allowed to restate the set. That is the same defect class one level up, bought for a live population of **1**. Axis ④ (创业阶段不扩散需求) says no, and the behavioural half is already pinned at `i18n-resolver.test.ts:3382`.

Declining to build a gate, **with the measurement that makes the decline checkable**, is the right output here. A gate that reproduces the defect it polices is worse than the comment it would have caught.

The population scan (7,660 tracked files → exactly **3** restatement sites) is what makes that argument sound rather than asserted: this PR's (fixed), the test header (filed as #15860), and `registry.ts:3039` — correctly fenced, since rewriting a retirement's recorded justification to match today's set would be the opposite mistake.

## One correction

The report notes the assignee field was empty on arrival and reads it as a PM-side half-state. It is **not** — this seat set it before dispatch, and it reads `os-litant` now. The likely cause is a page payload cached ahead of the write.

⚠️ But the handling was correct regardless, and for the designed reason: **the assignee field is no proof of who is working** — the shared identity makes it useless as one — so the claim comment is the identity bit. Treating a missing assignee as "not mine to trust" and proceeding from the claim comment is exactly right, and would have been right even if the field really had been empty.
